Days on which an entitlement was missed

Source: R/rvw.R
entcmp.Rd

The law may give a person held in a restrictive unit something every day: hours out of the cell, time with other people. entcmp() takes, for each stay, the percentage of its days on which that was missed, and gives the stays by how often it was missed, the share that missed it every day, and the share of all days missed. With the hours received on the days it was missed, it shows how far short those days fell; with the percentage of days the person refused, how many stays missed more days than refusal accounts for. These are the tables of Sprott and Doob (2021, Tables 6, 7, 14, 17 and 21) on the four hours out of cell and the two hours of human contact in Canada's Structured Intervention Units.

Usage

entcmp(
  miss,
  days = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  hours = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  cuts = c(20, 50),
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

miss

The percentage of the days of each stay on which the entitlement was missed: numbers from 0 to 100.

days

NULL, or the length of each stay in days (numbers from 0), for the share of all days missed.

by

NULL, or the group of each stay: labels.

hours

NULL, or the hours received on average on the days the entitlement was missed (numbers from 0; NA where none was missed).

ref

NULL, or the percentage of the days of each stay on which the person refused: numbers from 0 to 100.

cuts

The percentages that part the bands between never and always: increasing numbers above 0 and below 100.

level

The level of the exact intervals: one number between 0 and 1.

Value

A list: tab, a data frame with one row per group (then "all") and band (group, band, n, share); sum, one row per group (group, n, none the stays that never missed, all those that missed every day, share their share, lo, hi, half the stays that missed on half their days or more, dayshr the share of all days missed, NA without days); hrs (with hours), the stays that missed by the hours they received (band, n, share); ref (with ref), one row per group (group, n, most the stays that refused on more than half their days, net those that missed on more days than they refused); and level.

References

Sprott, J. B. and Doob, A. N. (2021). Solitary Confinement, Torture, and Canada's Structured Intervention Units. University of Toronto, Centre for Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, 23 February 2021.

Examples

miss <- c(100, 100, 80, 45, 10, 0, 100, 60)
entcmp(miss, days = c(20, 35, 16, 40, 18, 5, 62, 30),
       hours = c(0.4, 1.5, 2.2, 3, 3.5, NA, 0.8, 1),
       ref = c(10, 100, 5, 0, 0, 0, 30, 60))
#> $tab
#>   group                 band n share
#> 1   all                    0 1 0.125
#> 2   all         over 0 to 20 1 0.125
#> 3   all        over 20 to 50 1 0.125
#> 4   all over 50 to under 100 2 0.250
#> 5   all                  100 3 0.375
#> 
#> $sum
#>   group n none all share         lo        hi half    dayshr
#> 1   all 8    1   3 0.375 0.08523341 0.7551368    5 0.7415929
#> 
#> $hrs
#>            band n     share
#> 1     up to 0.5 1 0.1428571
#> 2 over 0.5 to 1 2 0.2857143
#> 3   over 1 to 2 1 0.1428571
#> 4   over 2 to 3 2 0.2857143
#> 5        over 3 1 0.1428571
#> 
#> $ref
#>   group n most net
#> 1   all 8    2   5
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
#>
